page: OVHcloud rtx5000-84 is a GPU-accelerated cloud instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. The host utilizes an x86_64 Intel Xeon W-3235 processor operating at 3.3 GHz, providing 16 dedicated physical cores without hyper-threading enabled. Compute capabilities are augmented by hardware support for AVX, AVX-512 Foundation, and AVX-512 VNNI. Memory capacity stands at 84.0 GB of system RAM, providing approximately 5.25 GB per core. The server includes a dedicated graphics subsystem comprising 3 NVIDIA Quadro RTX 5000 GPUs based on the Turing architecture, providing a combined total of 48 GB of GDDR6 VRAM. Storage consists of a local 400 GB SSD, accompanied by a 10 Gbps baseline network connection, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included by default.

Benchmark evaluations highlight the instance's strengths in GPU-accelerated machine learning workloads. In large language model inference, the server achieves top-tier results (top 10%) across prompt processing benchmarks, reaching 8884.89 tokens/sec on 135M models, 1827.36 tokens/sec on 7B models, and 220.48 tokens/sec on 70B models. Text generation benchmarks similarly demonstrate competitive performance, generating 65.53 tokens/sec on 7B models and 7.46 tokens/sec on 70B models. System memory performance registers a strong PassMark score of 2913.07, positioning it in the top 25%.

In contrast, standard host compute and I/O tasks fall primarily into average or lower performance tiers. General CPU workloads score in the middle 50%, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1473.0, a multi-core score of 8459.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 20742.83. Weaknesses emerge in write memory bandwidth for large blocks (25.38 GB/sec), single-threaded gzip compression (23.78 GB/sec), and Geekbench text processing (1387.0), all scoring in the bottom 25%. These characteristics confirm that the host CPU is intended primarily to support and feed data to the GPU cluster rather than handle standalone high-throughput data processing.

OVHcloud rtx5000-84 delivers high density in hardware accelerators, distributing 48 GB of total GPU memory across three independent accelerators. This configuration provides a cost-effective alternative to single ultra-high-end accelerator instances for parallel training batches, model inference, and distributed graphics rendering. Tradeoffs include modest local disk storage at 400 GB and lack of hyper-threading. The system is well matched for AI model inference, medium-scale deep learning workflows, ray tracing, video transcoding, and 3D rendering pipelines.
description: OVHcloud rtx5000-84 is a GPU-accelerated instance featuring 16 dedicated cores from an Intel Xeon W-3235 processor running at 3.3 GHz, paired with 84.0 GB of system RAM. Its primary processing capability comes from 3 bundled NVIDIA Quadro RTX 5000 GPUs, offering a combined 48 GB of VRAM. Networking features a 10 Gbps baseline, and local storage provides 400 GB on SSD. Benchmark data positions the server in the top 10% for LLM prompt processing and text generation across small, medium, and large models. In contrast, CPU-bound tasks such as multi-core processing and uncached memory writes register within average or bottom-tier brackets. The system offers efficient resource allocation for multi-GPU parallelization, making it suited for machine learning inference, computer vision, 3D ray tracing, and specialized rendering pipelines.
